source: Granular, revocable consent (challenge brief). Each purpose is asked where it matters (research: ask only what is needed, and say why), nothing is pre-ticked, and every purpose except care-team access can be changed later on 'See or delete your data'. Every change is appended to consent_records and written to the audit trail. One-line explanations are DRAFT; the psychiatrist and the licensed provider approve the final text.

purposes.title: My care team can see my answers
purposes.explanation: A licensed clinician reads your answers and chooses your next step with you. This is needed to use the check-in.

purposes.title: Use the AI assistant to help me answer
purposes.explanation: It asks a few questions in a chat. It is not a therapist and never diagnoses. Without it, you answer the questions on their own.

purposes.title: Phone calls
purposes.explanation: Your care team may call you.

purposes.title: SMS
purposes.explanation: Your care team may text you.

purposes.title: WhatsApp
purposes.explanation: Your care team may message you on WhatsApp.

purposes.title: Email
purposes.explanation: Your care team may email you.

purposes.title: Share my physical health with my care team
purposes.explanation: Long-term conditions and medicines can affect mood and sleep, so your clinician can take them into account.

purposes.title: Share a summary with my family doctor
purposes.explanation: You or your clinician can download it for your doctor. Nothing is sent automatically.

purposes.title: Check in again in about 4 weeks
purposes.explanation: A short check-in later, so you and your clinician can see how things change. You can stop at any time.

purposes.title: Anonymous service statistics
purposes.explanation: Your answers, with nothing that identifies you, help us check the service works fairly for everyone.
